home.hadith_text: O young boy, I shall teach you some words: Be mindful of Allah, and He will protect you. Be mindful of Allah, and you will find Him before you. When you ask, ask Allah; and when you seek help, seek help from Allah. Know that if the entire nation were to gather together to benefit you with anything, they would not benefit you except with something that Allah has already decreed for you. And if they were to gather together to harm you with anything, they would not harm you except with something that Allah has already decreed against you. The pens have been lifted, and the pages have dried.
home.hadith_source: Narrated by Jami' at-Tirmidhi (Hadith 2516), from Abdullah ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them)

pillars.heading: The Five Pillars of Islam
pillars.intro: Ibn Umar (may Allah be pleased with them) reported that the Prophet ﷺ said Islam is built upon five. Select a pillar to read more.
pillars.hadith: Hadith of the pillars of Islam

shahada.name: The Two Testimonies
shahada.short: Testifying that none has the right to be worshipped but Allah and that Muhammad is His messenger.
shahada.detail: The Muslim testifies that none is worthy of worship except Allah and that Muhammad ﷺ is His servant and messenger. It is the entrance to Islam, and fulfilling it means understanding its meaning, being sincere to Allah and following His Messenger.

salah.name: Establishing the Prayer
salah.short: The five daily prayers, a link between the servant and his Lord.
salah.detail: Allah made five prayers obligatory each day and night: Fajr, Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib and Isha. They are performed at their set times, in a state of purity and facing the Qibla. Its pillars, obligatory and recommended acts are covered in the “Pillars of Salah” section.

zakat.name: Giving Zakat
zakat.short: An obligatory due on wealth that reaches the minimum threshold, given to those entitled to it.
zakat.detail: Zakat is an obligatory act of worship concerning wealth, due on anyone whose wealth reaches the nisab and has been held for a lunar year, under its conditions. It is given to the eight categories mentioned by Allah in Surat at-Tawba; it purifies wealth and soul and supports solidarity in society.

sawm.name: Fasting Ramadan
sawm.short: Abstaining from what breaks the fast, from dawn to sunset, throughout the month of Ramadan.
sawm.detail: Every able Muslim fasts the month of Ramadan by abstaining from food, drink and other things that break the fast, from dawn until sunset, with the intention to fast. The sick and the traveller are allowed to break the fast and make up the missed days. The aim of fasting is God-consciousness (taqwa).

hajj.name: Pilgrimage (Hajj)
hajj.short: Travelling to the Sacred House of Allah to perform the rites, once in a lifetime for those who are able.
hajj.detail: Hajj is an act of worship performed in Makkah and its surroundings during the months of Hajj. It is obligatory once in a lifetime for the Muslim who is mature, sane and physically and financially able. Its rites include ihram, tawaf, sa’i and standing at Arafah.

salah.heading: Pillars of Salah
salah.intro: Learn the pillars of prayer in order, then tell them apart from the obligatory and recommended acts.
salah.school: The counting and classification of the prayer’s pillars differ between the schools of Islamic jurisprudence. This section presents the classification of the Hanbali school (fourteen pillars and eight obligatory acts) as found in the two sources listed below; what you learned in your own school may differ. For further study or in case of difference, consult a trusted scholar.

kindDesc.pillar: Pillar: the prayer is invalid without it, and it cannot be made up by the prostration of forgetfulness.
kindDesc.obligatory: Obligatory act: if forgotten, it is made up by the prostration of forgetfulness; leaving it on purpose invalidates the prayer.
kindDesc.sunnah: Recommended act (Sunnah): encouraged, and the prayer remains valid without it.

salah.obligatoryIntro: In this school there are eight obligatory acts, distinct from the pillars.
salah.sunnahIntro: Examples of recommended acts, not an exhaustive list; the fiqh books mention others.
salah.compareIntro: Three levels of acts in the prayer:

items.qiyam: Praying the obligatory prayer standing if able; if unable, praying seated, and if unable, on one’s side.
items.takbir: Saying “Allahu akbar” to begin the prayer; with it the worshipper enters the state of prayer.
items.fatiha: Reciting Surat al-Fatiha in the prayer.
items.ruku: Bowing in the prayer, in glorification of Allah.
items.itidal: Rising from the bowing to stand upright.
items.sujud: Placing the forehead (with the nose), both hands, both knees and the toes of both feet on the ground: the seven limbs.
items.tuma: Stillness in every physical pillar of the prayer, so that each limb settles in its place.
items.tashahhud: Reciting the tashahhud at the end of the prayer.
items.julus: Sitting to recite the final tashahhud.
items.salawat: Sending blessings upon the Prophet ﷺ in the final tashahhud.
items.taslim: The salutation to the right and then to the left, ending the prayer.
items.tartib: Performing the pillars of the prayer in the order established in the Sunnah.
items.takbirat: The takbirs in the prayer other than the opening one, such as when moving between positions.
items.tasmi: Said by the imam and by one praying alone when rising from the bowing.
items.tahmid: Said after rising from the bowing.
items.tasbih_ruku: The obligatory glorification in the bowing, once.
items.tasbih_sujud: The obligatory glorification in the prostration, once.
items.rabbighfir: Said while sitting between the two prostrations.
items.tashahhud1: The tashahhud recited in the middle sitting of three- and four-rak’a prayers.
items.julus1: Sitting to recite the first tashahhud.
items.raf_yadayn: One of the recommended acts of the prayer mentioned in the fiqh books.
items.istiftah: One of the recommended acts of the prayer mentioned in the fiqh books.
items.surah: One of the recommended acts of the prayer mentioned in the fiqh books.
items.tasbih_more: One of the recommended acts of the prayer mentioned in the fiqh books.

morning.title: Morning Adhkar
morning.intro: Recited after the Fajr prayer until sunrise; they may still be recited later in the day if the time was missed.

evening.title: Evening Adhkar
evening.intro: Recited after the Asr prayer until sunset; the time extends into the night.
